title: B. L. Mitter
summary: Describes the States as integral to India, supports a strong Union and argues that constitutional design must accommodate institutional variety.

title: K. M. Panikkar
summary: Treats the arrival of State representatives as a historic act of voluntary national association and rejects claims of coercion.

title: P. Govinda Menon
summary: Argues that the people of the States see themselves as Indians and highlights Cochin's elected participation and commitment to remain within India.

title: Jawaharlal Nehru
summary: Reports negotiations with the Chamber of Princes, explains the representation compromise and defends practical entry of States representatives into the Assembly.

title: Somnath Lahiri
summary: Asks how many State representatives were elected rather than nominated and protests that late notice prevented amendments to the States Committee motion.

title: G. Durgabai
summary: Moves to add two representatives of Indian States to the Steering Committee instead of leaving all reserved places vacant while participation expands.

title: N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar
summary: Presents the Union-subject report but argues that political uncertainty requires postponing debate and may force a later overhaul of federal powers.
